hints: Focus on why immunity is easy to build against smallpox but hard against malaria. Think about what happens if a pathogen keeps changing its surface antigens.
Check each numbered statement one by one. Remember that vaccines can protect against bacteria as well as viruses, for example tetanus and diphtheria vaccines.
walkthrough:
**Think about what makes eradication possible**

To eradicate a disease we need long lasting immunity in the population, usually from a very effective vaccine. That works best when the pathogen has stable antigens that do not change.

Smallpox virus fits this perfectly, so one vaccine gave solid protection worldwide.

**Check statements 2 and 3 about antigens**

Statement 3 is true. Smallpox antigens remain stable, so memory cells made after vaccination always recognise the virus later.

Statement 2 is also true. Plasmodium, which causes malaria, changes its antigens during its complex life cycle in liver, red blood cells and mosquito. The immune system struggles to keep up, so making an effective long lasting vaccine is very difficult.

**Check statements 1 and 4 about treatment and vaccines**

Statement 1 is true. Cholera bacteria (Vibrio cholerae) live in the lumen of the intestines where antibiotics in the blood reach them poorly, so antibiotics do not reliably destroy them and the bacteria keep spreading in faeces and dirty water.

Statement 4 is false. Vaccines do not only work against viruses. They also work against many bacteria, for example cholera, tetanus, diphtheria and tuberculosis. So 4 cannot explain the difference.

**Put it together**

Correct explanations are 1, 2 and 3 only. That matches option A.

options.A: Correct, because 1, 2 and 3 are all true and explain why smallpox was eradicated but malaria and cholera were not, while 4 is false.
options.B: Incorrect, because it includes statement 4 which is false. Vaccines work against bacteria as well as viruses.
options.C: Incorrect, because it includes statement 4 which is false, even though 1 and 3 are true.
options.D: Incorrect, because it includes statement 4 which is false and leaves out true statement 1 about cholera and antibiotics.
